motion.name: section-flow-pattern

motion.purpose: Faded reference-style square grid in WhoAmISection. Short gradient pulses travel left-to-right and top-to-bottom along aligned grid lines. Pauses offscreen/in hidden tabs; reduced motion retains only the static grid.

Prop: scrollYProgress (MotionValue<number>). Usage: <ContactHeader scrollYProgress={scrollYProgress} />. A module-level motion.create(Stack) wrapper accepts the opacity and vertical MotionValues directly, without type assertions. ContactForm email also uses overflow-wrap: anywhere.
responsive.process: ProcessSection has no fixed mobile height and a 750px desktop minimum. ProcessCard grows with text; padding is 16px below 600px and 32px above. Image minimum height: 220px at xs, 240px at sm, 180px at md. Optional ProcessCard imagePosition (center by default, or bottom) controls contained image alignment. responsive.biography: WhoAmISection uses a flexible text column and 320px square portrait at 900px and above. Below 900px, the portrait follows the introduction and sole project action and is capped at 360px; service columns stack. The project action reuses AnimatedTextLink to link to #works and uses intrinsic width, 16px semibold brick text via a section-specific semanticColors.actionSecondary override, a 20px right arrow and a 44px minimum height. Its 2px underline scales from left to right over 280ms on hover or keyboard focus, immediately for reduced motion. It retains a visible focus outline and an unfilled surface. The section omits its contact CTA and retains a 96px anchor offset. On hover or keyboard focus, its arrow moves 3px horizontally and back in a repeating 1600ms ease-in-out cycle; it stops on leaving the interaction and is disabled for reduced motion. FlowPattern spans the complete section at every breakpoint behind the content; its clipped layers cannot cause page overflow. The portrait-local DotPattern is removed.

imageLoading.heroPreload: Only FitNLit is preloaded, with media (min-width: 900px); getImageProps shares its srcset/sizes with the actual image props. Mobile collage and other portfolio imagery use lazy loading.
imageLoading.modal: src/components/FullScreenImageModal/index.tsx: props isOpen, onClose, imageUrl?, alt?. Usage: <FullScreenImageModal isOpen={open} onClose={close} imageUrl={url} alt={alt} />. sizes: (min-width: 964px) 900px, calc(100vw - 64px); default quality 75.

Optional imagePosition: center | bottom (default center). Usage: <ProcessCard title={title} description={description} imageUrl="/services/design.webp" alt={alt} imagePosition="bottom" />. composition.biography: `src/components/WhoAmISection/index.tsx`: server-rendered, localized introduction for prospective clients. No props; usage: `<WhoAmISection />`. A two-part `h2`, short introduction, project anchor link, and portrait precede three open, divider-led service columns: end-to-end development, AI-powered products/automation, and agentic coding with human engineering oversight. No individual project examples or metrics appear here. Desktop uses a flexible text column and 320px square portrait; below 900px the portrait follows the introduction and project action, and service columns stack. The portrait caps at 360px on mobile. The sole action reuses `AnimatedTextLink` to link to `#works`, with a section-specific `semanticColors.actionSecondary` override for 16px semibold brick text, a 20px right arrow, and a 44px minimum height. A 2px underline scales from left to right over 280ms on hover or keyboard focus; the arrow moves 3px horizontally and back in a repeating 1600ms ease-in-out cycle during the same interaction. Leaving hover/focus returns it to rest. Reduced motion makes the underline immediate and disables arrow movement. The link retains a visible focus outline, intrinsic width and an unfilled surface. The contact CTA is omitted from this section. The section retains `id="about"`, adds a named section landmark and 96px anchor offset, and uses semantic color tokens. Entrance and portrait motion stay in the existing `FadeInItem` and `RevealItem` client components; `FlowPattern` supplies a full-section square grid fading toward all edges, with paired heartbeat pulses traveling left-to-right and top-to-bottom along grid lines, paused offscreen/in hidden tabs and static for reduced motion, replacing the portrait-local DotPattern; CTA interaction styles live in `AnimatedTextLink`; service copy is visible without entrance animation. Copy lives under matching `who_am_i_section` keys in both locale files.
composition.projects: src/components/MyWorksSection/index.tsx and src/app/[locale]/projects/page.tsx select locale and full project data on the server. MyWorksSection takes no props, usage <MyWorksSection />. Cards receive serializable title, description, images, href and optional animationDirection.
composition.boundaries: MyWorkCard, FadeInItem and RevealItem explicitly declare use client. MyWorkCard requires href instead of the former onClick navigation callback, using the existing locale-aware Link. Entrance timing and reduced-motion behavior stay unchanged.
composition.process: src/components/ProcessSection/index.tsx and ProcessCard render on the server; ProcessSection has no props, usage <ProcessSection /> and getTranslations for localized copy.
composition.animatedTextLink: src/components/AnimatedTextLink/index.tsx is a client component rendering a native MUI link by default. Required props: children, href. Optional icon replaces the default right arrow; icon={null} hides it. Standard MUI Link props (excluding underline) plus sx style overrides are supported. Usage: <AnimatedTextLink href="#works">Explore my work</AnimatedTextLink>. WhoAmISection delegates all project CTA styles and interactions to this component. WhoAmISection overrides sx.color with semanticColors.actionSecondary (brick); icon and underline inherit it. The reusable default and focus ring remain navy.
composition.flowPattern: src/components/FlowPattern/index.tsx: decorative client component, no props; usage <FlowPattern /> in a positioned, isolated section with content at zIndex 1. Full-bounds aria-hidden, pointer-transparent clipped layer at zIndex 0. Stationary 1px square grid with 7.5% navy alpha; cells 64px below 900px and 96px above. A radial ellipse at 50%/55% fades the grid toward all edges, following the supplied reference on white. Two horizontal tracks at rows 3 and 9/6 (mobile/desktop), and two vertical tracks at columns 2/4 and 5/10, carry paired 144px gradient segments with 28% peak navy alpha and 650ms spacing. Each 10-second cycle travels forward for 4.8s then pauses. Track delays: horizontal 0/4s, vertical 2/6s. Only transforms and opacity animate. useInView and document visibility pause offscreen/hidden animation; reduced motion hides pulse tracks and retains the static grid. An intersected vertical mask fades the grid and pulses below 40% section height to 35% opacity at 60% and fully transparent at 76%, keeping capability divider lines distinct.

narrative.overview:
The interface is a clean, contemporary, light-first portfolio that earns attention through project imagery, generous whitespace, clear typography, and restrained motion. It should feel modern and technically capable without resembling a generic software dashboard or relying on visual hype.

The geometric POLAT logo establishes a navy-and-brick identity. Deep navy gives the interface authority and makes primary actions feel deliberate; brick adds entrepreneurial energy in restrained signals. White remains dominant so the work stays central and the identity feels established rather than loud.
keyCharacteristics: Spacious, image-led compositions with strong text hierarchy.
Authority navy for actions and emphasis, with restrained brick signals against white.
Softly rounded project surfaces with subtle, low-contrast depth.
Purposeful reveal and scroll motion that never competes with the work.

rules.name: The Navy Leads Rule
rules.body: Navy owns actions, links, focus, and primary emphasis. Brick is a controlled signal for the logo and selected highlights; it never competes with navy as a second primary CTA color.

rules.name: The Contrast Rule
rules.body: Use white on navy and brick. Supporting Slate is only used on white or equivalently light surfaces; Authority Ink carries primary text.

rules.name: Flat by default
rules.body: Use shadow only to clarify layering, interaction, or a featured composition.

rules.name: No button shadows
rules.body: Buttons, including CTAs, navigation buttons, and icon buttons, must remain shadow-free in default, hover, pressed, focused, and disabled states. Do not use colored halos or elevation to attract attention to an action. Use color, contrast, borders, and spacing; retain visible focus outlines. This user preference also applies to future components and overrides generic button-elevation examples.

dos: **Do** let project imagery and shipped work provide the visual proof.
**Do** let Authority Navy lead actions, links, and focus.
**Do** use Entrepreneurial Brick sparingly for recognition and selected signals.
**Do** preserve generous whitespace and clear bilingual hierarchy.
**Do** keep motion smooth, controlled, and supportive of reading order.
donts: **Don't** add shadows, colored glows, or hover elevation to buttons or CTAs.
**Don't** turn brick into a competing primary action color or use it decoratively everywhere.
**Don't** fabricate testimonials, results, client claims, or project metrics.
**Don't** introduce gratuitous gradients, neon effects, or generic technology-dashboard styling.
**Don't** make every surface a card or use shadow as decoration.
**Don't** let interactive or 3D elements compete with the portfolio and contact journey.
